text:
The evidence shows tree-cover loss in 2023, but it does not establish deforestation.

- Hansen/UMD mapped about 0.7 ha of tree-cover loss in 2023, roughly 1.2% of the 58.1 ha asset. A later year was observed and the JRC 2020 map agrees the area was forest, so the loss is corroborated.
- The MGAP 2021 map shows the affected area is mostly planted forest (0.4 ha of eucalyptus) and the rest (0.3 ha) is outside mapped forest. None of it is native forest. This is context only, not a cause.
- The tree-cover loss measure counts any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation. That is why it can't confirm deforestation or land-use change.
- The data also don't show the cause, legality, responsible party, or any compliance status.

The evidence is consistent with plantation harvest, but it doesn't prove that. Establishing whether this was deforestation would need land-use information after the loss, such as whether the area was replanted or converted.
